description: Derives service capability FLAGS from an AWS Threat Model threat model, scanning mitigation STATEMENTS only — never entity descriptions/information prose. A mitigation statement is a normative assertion about how the service must be configured ('An AWS Lambda function should be encrypted with a KMS CMK'); an entity 'information' field is descriptive marketing prose ('a custom runtime ... reused across functions') that must never assert a customer capability. Each flag is three-valued: present (a statement positively asserts the capability), absent (a statement asserts the capability is NOT the customer's to control, e.g. AWS-managed), or unknown (neither — the export is silent). Downstream, unknown NEVER forces an objective N/A; it defers to the KB default. Consumed by scripts/compute-applicability-matrix.py.
polarity_note: present_when matches a statement that asserts the customer configures/controls the capability. absent_when matches a statement that asserts the capability is out of the customer's hands (AWS-managed). If both match, absent wins (a service can mention a capability only to say AWS owns it). If neither matches, the flag is unknown — not present and not absent.

capability_rules.description: Customer supplies/controls a KMS customer-managed key for encryption at rest.
Service can be placed in a customer VPC / subnets / ENIs / security groups.
Service can be spread across more than one Availability Zone by the customer.
Service supports / requires TLS encryption of data in transit under customer control.
Service emits access/activity logs the customer can enable (CloudWatch Logs, CloudTrail data events).
Service assumes a customer-controlled IAM execution/service role.
present_when: service role should only be assumable
role should be accessed only by trusted

capability_rules.description: Service exposes a resource-based policy / version policy the customer scopes.
present_when: permissions to a subset of iam principals

capability_rules.description: Service has a public-access surface that can be misconfigured (function URL, resource policy).
Service supports code-signing of deployment artifacts (code integrity, NOT data-in-transit).
Service resources can be tagged for attribution/classification.

Customer is responsible for OS/software patching of the service's runtime. Serverless/fully-managed services are patched by AWS — this flag must NOT fire from a descriptive mention of a 'custom runtime' or 'operating system'; only a statement placing patching responsibility on the customer counts.
absent_when: no operating system for the customer to patch

capability_rules.description: Service exposes a customer-configurable backup/snapshot/PITR API.

present_when: replicated to at least one other aws region

capability_rules.description: Service owns durable storage the customer manages (objects, volumes, tables) — a data-at-rest store, not ephemeral compute state.

Service IS the log store (log group / trail / log bucket) whose modify/delete the customer can restrict — the surface LOG-02/LOG-09 (log protection) actually govern. A service that merely EMITS logs to CloudWatch does not own the log store; CloudWatch/CloudTrail do.
